brief.motion: Confident and cinematic: slow camera push, springy reveals with a small overshoot, light streaks on key beats, film grain. Every key visual lands on the word that names it.
brief.story: Before/after: plain office slides are shown as they are, then transformed. Dark stage for drama, one light paper scene for the how-it-works explanation, gradient finale.

scenes.narration: This video started life as five ordinary slides. Watch what happens when they get a director.

scenes.storyboard: the real input slides drop onto a dark stage as a flat row. On "ordinary" they drain of colour. On beat 2 the others fly off and slide 1 pushes to camera; a clapper snaps on "director", the slide flips and its back is the designed title card, which then grows to fill the frame.

scenes.narration: Most slide videos are just slides, with a voice reading out the bullet points. By slide three, your audience has tuned out.

slide.title: The problem
slide.text: Most slide videos are just slides and a voice. The bullet points get read aloud. Audiences tune out fast
slide.notes: Most slide videos are just slides, with a voice reading out the bullet points. By slide three, your audience has tuned out.

beats.text: Most slide videos are just slides, with a voice reading out the bullet points.

scenes.storyboard: the usual slide video, shown honestly: a player with the plain slide, a monotone waveform, bullets highlighted as they're read. An attention graph beside it sags. On "slide three" the counter ticks 1-2-3; on "tuned out" the line bottoms out in coral and the player goes dim.

scenes.narration: PowerPoint2Vid reads your whole deck. It writes the story, designs every scene, and times each animation to the narration.

scenes.storyboard: light paper scene (contrast after the dim player). A scan beam reads the stacked deck, then a path draws left to right and three cards pop exactly on "story", "scene" and "times": a script being written, a storyboard, and keyframes snapping to a waveform. Ends on a glowing play button on "narration".

scenes.narration: So a flat chart becomes a moment. The numbers build, and the result lands right as it's said.

scenes.storyboard: the deck's real default chart, shown as-is, literally tips flat on "flat". On "moment" it sinks away and the same data rises as glowing columns on a dark stage. Columns and counters build one by one on "numbers build"; on "result lands" Q4 ignites, the others dim and "+117%" slams in.

scenes.storyboard: finale on a drifting aurora. The promise is typeset word by word as it's spoken; "ordinary" stays muted and "extraordinary" ignites. On the URL a button lands, a cursor glides in and clicks it. Holds as an end card.
